results.title: ByteAsk: Build-Aware Context and a Checking Harness for C++ Coding Agents. ByteAsk Research
results.content:
Large language model (LLM) coding agents have changed how people write software: a developer describes a change in plain language and the agent finds, edits, and tests the code. Most of this progress, however, has concentrated on a few widely used languages, Python above all. C and C++, which still underpin operating systems, browsers, databases, and embedded software, remain far less explored, even though their large, build-dependent codebases are exactly the setting in which agents struggle to find where a change belongs. We propose ByteAsk, a coding agent built for C and C++. At its core is a context engine that understands a codebase the way the project's own build does. Before the model starts, the engine tells it where the change belongs, which related places may need the same [...] the change belongs, which related places may need the same change, and which tests cover them; ByteAsk then checks the change against only those tests. We compare ByteAsk with OpenAI's Codex CLI running the same underlying model, on recent issues from popular and little-known C++ projects and on a small set of hard issues. Both agents fix the same number of runs in every set (129 of 144 each, across the two main sets), but ByteAsk uses 63–80% fewer tokens and costs 59–70% less. [...] ## Key findings

1. 01Same fixes as Codex CLI on the same model: 129 of 144 runs fixed by each.
2. 0263–80% fewer tokens and 59–70% lower cost in every task set.
3. 03The biggest savings come on little-known and hard C++ projects: about 80% fewer tokens.

results.title: How Coding Agents Work in Slack | Slack
results.content:
Codex is a coding agent from OpenAI that runs everywhere you code — in your terminal, code editor, and the cloud. Codex understands complex codebases, plans and implements new features, debugs difficult issues, and provides high-signal code reviews to help your team ship faster and with more confidence.

Cursor helps you fix issues directly from Slack by starting coding agents. These agents can investigate bugs, add new features, update documentation, and more. Cloud agents can solve quick bugs or build ambitious ideas, with the ability to run for hours on the most complex tasks.
